title: What causes tropical cyclones

match.reason: Neither bank point explains what causes tropical cyclones: the flood point only defines a cyclone and covers floods and storm surges, and the hazard point covers what makes a natural hazard in general.

draft.title: What causes tropical cyclones
card: A tropical cyclone is a large, spinning storm with very strong winds and heavy rain. It forms over warm tropical seas.
Warm sea water evaporates, so the air above it becomes warm and moist. This air rises.
As the moist air rises, it cools and forms thick storm clouds. More warm, moist air flows in below to replace it, and the storm keeps being fed.
The Earth's spin makes the storm turn. A cyclone usually weakens once it moves over cooler water or over land, because the warm sea no longer feeds it.
draft.remember: Warm sea and rising moist air feed a spinning storm. Cut off from the warm sea, it weakens.

a.q: Why does a warm tropical sea help a cyclone to form?
opts: It adds warm, moist air that rises and feeds the storm
It makes the air above it cold and dry and pushes it down
It stops the Earth's spin so the storm can stay still
It carries the storm clouds in from the cooler land
a.why: Warm water evaporates into the air above it. This warm, moist air rises and feeds the storm. Cold, dry air would not give the storm the moisture it needs.
a.clue: Think about what warm water does to the air above it.

b.q: A cyclone off the coast of Queensland moves inland over dry land. What is most likely to happen to it, and why?
opts: It weakens, because it is cut off from the warm sea
It strengthens, because the land is warmer than the sea
It weakens, because the Earth's spin stops over land
It strengthens, because dry air rises faster than moist air
b.why: A cyclone is fed by warm, moist air rising from a warm sea. Over land it loses that supply, so it usually weakens. The Earth's spin does not stop over land, so that reason is wrong.
b.clue: What feeds the storm, and is it still there over land?

a.best: It adds warm, moist air that rises and feeds the storm

b.best: It weakens, because it is cut off from the warm sea
